articles.title: 'My parents came from India last night': Nikhil Chaudhary's emotional Player of the Match moment at MCG
articles.summary: For Nikhil Chaudhary, Saturday's memorable night at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) was about much more than scoring a match-winning 66 or picking up
articles.body: For Nikhil Chaudhary, Saturday's memorable night at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) was about much more than scoring a match-winning 66 or picking up two wickets against England. It was a special family moment as the Indian-born Australian all-rounder's parents travelled from India to watch him play for the first time, witnessing him deliver a Player of the Match performance in Australia's thrilling three-wicket victory.Born in Delhi, Chaudhary produced an outstanding all-round display in the first T20I against England, smashing 66 off just 38 deliveries before claiming two wickets for 21 runs in his four overs. His contribution helped Australia chase down England's 188-run target with one ball to spare.However, the biggest highlight for the 30-year-old came after the match when he reflected on his parents' presence at the MCG and admitted that he had never imagined receiving such an honour while representing Australia."My parents came over from India last night, so there's nothing better than getting a Man of the Match against them, and it's their first game watching me play as well," Chaudhary said after the match.'Never imagined that': Chaudhary reflects on special MCG momentAsked whether he had ever imagined becoming Player of the Match for Australia at the MCG, the all-rounder admitted that it was something he had never anticipated."No, man, never imagined that," he said, before highlighting how special it was to have his parents witness the performance.Nikhil Chaudhary stars in Australia's thrilling winChaudhary delivered an outstanding all-round performance, scoring 66 off just 38 deliveries, including five fours and two sixes. His innings proved crucial in Australia's successful chase of 188.The 30-year-old had also made an impact with the ball, claiming two wickets for just 21 runs in his four overs. He dismissed England captain Harry Brook, who top-scored with an explosive 65 off 28 deliveries, and Sam Curran, who contributed 21.Earlier, England posted 187/9 in their 20 overs after being asked to bat. Brook and Tom Banton, who scored 39, helped the visitors recover from an early setback and build a competitive total. Jordan Cox added 27, while Liam Dawson chipped in with 17. For Australia, Jack Edwards picked up two wickets, while Joel Davies, Riley Meredith, Ben Dwarshuis and Adam Zampa claimed one each.In reply, Australia got off to a shaky start after Jake Fraser-McGurk was dismissed for one, but Sam Harper (32) and captain Mitchell Marsh (37) steadied the innings.Chaudhary then took charge with his aggressive strokeplay, forming an important partnership with Tim David, who scored 20. After his dismissal for 66, Jack Edwards remained unbeaten on 25 to guide Australia home.The hosts eventually reached 191/7 in 19.5 overs, securing a three-wicket victory with one ball remaining. Chaudhary was named Player of the Match for his outstanding contribution with both bat and ball.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Big blow for Bangladesh! Star player ruled out of second Test against South Africa
articles.summary: Bangladesh have suffered a major setback ahead of the second Test against South Africa, with experienced batter Mushfiqur Rahim ruled out of the series
articles.body: Bangladesh have suffered a major setback ahead of the second Test against South Africa, with experienced batter Mushfiqur Rahim ruled out of the series finale due to a groin injury.The second Test is scheduled to begin at Centurion on November 23, with Bangladesh needing a victory to level the two-match series after going 1-0 down in Johannesburg.Mushfiqur sustained the injury during the opening Test at the Wanderers, where he complained of acute pain in his left groin. A subsequent MRI scan confirmed inflammation and irritation around the bony pelvis, forcing the team management to rule him out of the upcoming contest.Bangladesh national team physiotherapist Bayjedul Islam Khan confirmed the development, explaining that the veteran batter needs immediate rest and a rehabilitation programme to prevent the injury from worsening."Mushfiqur complained of acute pain in the left groin region during the first Test match. Following the Test, he underwent an MRI scan and the results confirmed some inflammation and irritation around the bony pelvis," Khan said."He requires immediate rest and targeted rehabilitation to manage the stress response and prevent further aggravation and is unavailable for the second Test," he added.Mushfiqur's absence comes at a difficult time for Bangladesh, who will be keen to bounce back after suffering a nine-wicket defeat in the series opener. The veteran batter had scored 22 in the first innings and 22 in the second innings of the Johannesburg Test.Meanwhile, South Africa have also been dealt an injury setback, with captain Temba Bavuma ruled out of the second Test due to a calf strain. Bavuma is expected to remain with the squad, while Aiden Markram is likely to take over the captaincy. Tony de Zorzi is tipped to come into the playing XI as his replacement.Bangladesh face uphill task to level seriesThe opening Test at the Wanderers saw Bangladesh produce a spirited fightback after an early batting collapse. From 22/3 and later 121/5, they recovered through centuries from Towhid Hridoy (137) and Litton Das (120), who put together a record 206-run partnership for the sixth wicket to take the visitors to 400.South Africa responded with a formidable 557, powered by maiden Test centuries from Marques Ackerman (157) and Ryan Rickelton (102), while Zubayr Hamza contributed 83 and Kagiso Rabada struck a career-best 72.Bangladesh fought back with the ball, but South Africa secured a sizeable 157-run first-innings advantage.In their second innings, the visitors struggled against Rabada and Simon Harmer, eventually being bowled out for 168. Harmer was the chief destroyer with figures of 6/51, while Rabada claimed three wickets.South Africa were left with a modest target of 12 runs and completed the chase to register a nine-wicket victory, taking a 1-0 lead in the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Make history by winning three titles in a row': RCB head coach's big statement ahead of IPL 2027
articles.summary: Defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru are confident of maintaining their winning combination as they prepare for the IPL 2027 auction, despite
articles.body: Defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru are confident of maintaining their winning combination as they prepare for the IPL 2027 auction, despite having considerably less spending power than several of their rivals.RCB, who clinched their second consecutive title by defeating Gujarat Titans by five wickets in the final in Ahmedabad this year, are targeting an unprecedented third straight IPL crown.Head coach Andy Flower said the franchise was satisfied with the core of its squad and was under no pressure to make sweeping changes at the auction, scheduled to take place in Goa on December 16.RCB have retained the bulk of their title-winning group, with Virat Kohli, Josh Hazlewood, Phil Salt and skipper Rajat Patidar among those staying on. The franchise released just five players, including injured England all-rounder Jacob Bethell, leaving them with Rs 14.15 crore to fill five available slots, one of which is reserved for an overseas player."We have had two very strong years, and going into the third year of this cycle, we are very confident and comfortable with the squad we have," Flower said on JioStar's 'TATA IPL 2027 Retention Special'.While acknowledging the need to use the auction to improve the squad, Flower admitted that RCB would have limited financial flexibility compared to other franchises."We have made a few releases and the responsibility at an auction is always to improve your squad, and we will be looking to do that."But we will be more limited than some of the other sides in the auction when it comes to spending power."We are comfortable with that because we have retained the bulk of our squad and a very strong core, the players who have served us so well over the last couple of years. We will be looking for that combination to work well again for us in 2027, and we have a very important season ahead where we can make history by winning three titles in a row."GT explain decision to release IshantMeanwhile, Gujarat Titans assistant coach Parthiv Patel acknowledged that parting ways with experienced India pacer Ishant Sharma was a difficult call, given the influence he had within the dressing room.Ishant, who spent the last two seasons with the franchise, did not feature in a single match last season. GT also released Luke Wood and Connor Esterhuizen as they looked to make changes to their squad."It is not the easiest of decisions to let go of players, but Ishant Sharma has been with us for the last two seasons, and he was such a great influence on the players."For a player who has played 100 Test matches for India to then not get a game in an IPL season is something that is difficult. The same goes for Luke Wood and Connor Esterhuizen. That is the main reason why we have let go of certain players."We also have to see that in this three-year cycle since the last mega auction, we have had a good bit of success. We qualified for the playoffs in 2025, we played in the final last season, so there was not much need to let go of a high number of players. We are quite happy with the way things are at the moment as far as our team combination is concerned, so we have not let go of many players," he said.GT have brought in Harshal Patel from Sunrisers Hyderabad through a trade, with Parthiv identifying the experienced pacer as the answer to the void left by Ishant.The Gujarat-born bowler's familiarity with local conditions, coupled with his death-over expertise, made him an important addition to the squad, Parthiv said."Harshal Patel's inclusion is an important addition for us. We have let go of the experience of Ishant Sharma, so we needed someone with that kind of experience in our squad. Harshal is also a player who is from Gujarat. He understands these conditions really well. On top of everything, he brings a lot of quality. He brings that death-bowling specialist role, which we were always looking for," he said.Highlighting Harshal's consistency and ability to handle pressure, Parthiv added that his variations would give the team another reliable option in the closing stages of an innings."His record in the IPL speaks for itself. He has been one of the most consistent wicket-takers in the death overs, and he knows how to bowl on flat wickets and in pressure situations. He also brings that experience of playing big matches, which helps the younger bowlers in the squad."With his variations and his ability to bowl the yorker and the slower ball, he gives us a strong option at the back end of the innings. That is exactly what we needed after losing an experienced campaigner like Ishant. When you have a local player like that and the opportunity comes up, that is the reason why we traded for Harshal to bring him into our team," he added.KKR look to add batting firepowerKolkata Knight Riders, meanwhile, have identified their batting department as the primary area requiring attention ahead of the auction.Head coach Abhishek Nayar said the franchise had explored the trade market but would now look to use the auction to bring in the firepower needed to strengthen the batting line-up."Batting is a department we want to strengthen. You try your hand at trades and hope that it works, but sometimes when it does not, you want to go into the auction and get the kind of firepower that can strengthen your batting," Nayar said.Nayar was satisfied with KKR's bowling performances, pointing out that the team had topped the rankings for wickets taken and performed consistently across different phases of the game."With regard to bowling, I felt we did really well. We were the number-one-ranked team when it came to picking up wickets and doing well in different phases of the game. But batting is an aspect we definitely want to strengthen."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Bigger than Hansie Cronje's match-fixing': Legendary cricketer makes explosive Sandpaper Gate claim
articles.summary: England great Geoffrey Boycott has launched a fresh attack on former Australia captain Steven Smith over his involvement in the infamous 2018 Sandpaper
articles.body: England great Geoffrey Boycott has launched a fresh attack on former Australia captain Steven Smith over his involvement in the infamous 2018 Sandpaper Gate scandal, insisting that history should judge him harshly for failing to prevent the ball-tampering plot.Boycott believes Smith cannot escape responsibility by claiming he chose not to involve himself in the plan after it was discussed by his teammates. The former Australian skipper was present when David Warner suggested using abrasive material to generate reverse swing and Cameron Bancroft agreed to carry out the act. However, rather than intervening, Smith told the team that he did not want to know anything further about it.In his column for The Telegraph, Boycott argued that Smith had failed in his primary duty as captain by allowing the plan to proceed.“As captain, Smith should have put a stop to it as soon as Warner raised the idea of using sandpaper," Boycott wrote.“For him to say ‘I don’t want to know about it’, yet let it go ahead and accept the unfair benefits of cheating and think that somehow it absolved him as not being part of it is staggering. History should not be kind to Smith. He abrogated his responsibility as a captain."Smith had accepted responsibility for his involvement and served a one-year ban imposed by Cricket Australia. According to Usman Khawaja, who revisited the controversy in his book Sabr, Smith took the punishment in an attempt to shield his teammates.'Bigger than Hansie Cronje's match-fixing'Boycott also offered a strong assessment of the scale of the scandal, claiming it was even more damaging than the match-fixing controversy involving former South Africa captain Hansie Cronje in 2000.While there has been debate over whether Cricket Australia's punishment was excessive, given that ball-tampering has long been a part of cricket and is covered under ICC regulations, Boycott believes the Sandpaper Gate episode was unprecedented.Cronje was stripped of the South African captaincy and eventually received a lifetime ban after admitting to accepting money from bookmakers to influence matches.However, Boycott argued that the Australian scandal was more extensive because it involved an entire team rather than a handful of individuals.“The sandpaper scandal is even bigger than Hansie Cronje’s match-fixing, which ripped apart South Africa cricket more than 25 years ago. This is bigger than anything I have read or seen in cricket: a whole team cheating. Cronje’s crimes mainly involved him recruiting a couple of junior players… but sandpaper involved the whole Australian team. The squad and coaches were all up to their necks in it, plotting and planning to cheat en masse, and the cover-up let three players take the blame," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Fighter jet gestures: Umpire celebrates with Pakistan team after controversial Asia Cup win; India questions neutrality
articles.summary: The Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI) has questioned the neutrality of a Pakistani umpire after a video appeared to show him celebrating
articles.body: The Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI) has questioned the neutrality of a Pakistani umpire after a video appeared to show him celebrating with Pakistan players through gestures that seemed to mimic aircrafts crashing. The incident has added to the tensions between the two teams following the controversy over the rain-hit Men's Asia Cup for the Blind final in Dhaka.India's blind cricket team had boycotted the trophy presentation ceremony after Pakistan were declared champions despite the final being washed out without a ball being bowled. CABI has now raised concerns over the umpire's conduct, saying match officials must remain neutral and should not be seen celebrating with either team.“This Pakistani umpire officiated throughout the Asia Cup Cricket for the Blind 2026, yet is seen celebrating with the Pakistan team,” CABI said in a statement.“As per the principles of officiating, an umpire must remain neutral and should never be seen aligning with any team,” the association added.The latest row follows Pakistan being awarded the title on the basis of a superior run rate after rain prevented the final from taking place. India had argued that both teams should have been declared joint winners, as there was no reserve day, instead of deciding the title through net run rate.The controversy grew after World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC) president and Pakistan Blind Cricket Council chief Sultan Shah reportedly overruled the WBCC Technical Committee's recommendation to declare India and Pakistan joint winners. The match referee was then directed to announce Pakistan as champions.CABI general secretary Shailendra Yadav accused Pakistan of unilaterally declaring themselves champions, alleging that the decision disregarded the position of the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC) Technical Committee."I am deeply disappointed and strongly condemn the manner in which Pakistan has declared itself the winner of the Blind Cricket Asia Cup final without a single ball being bowled," Yadav said in a statement.In protest, the Indian players stayed away from the trophy presentation ceremony.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rishabh Pant scripts history, joins Sachin, Dravid, Kohli in elite list with record-breaking century in Wellington
articles.summary: Box-office Rishabh Pant was at his brutal best against New Zealand in the first Test in Wellington, smashing 128 off 153 balls to take India to 629/6 at
articles.body: Box-office Rishabh Pant was at his brutal best against New Zealand in the first Test in Wellington, smashing 128 off 153 balls to take India to 629/6 at lunch on Day 4 on Sunday. Pant was caught in the deep just before the break, but not before helping India extend their lead to 261 runs.With this century, Pant became the sixth Indian batter to score a Test hundred in a SENA country, joining Mohammad Azharuddin, Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul on the list.He also became the ninth Asian batter to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries.Asian batters with Test hundreds in all four SENA countriesMohammad AzharuddinSachin TendulkarSaeed AnwarRahul DravidYounis KhanKumar SangakkaraVirat KohliKL RahulRishabh PantPant also moved to third place on the list of most Test centuries by a designated wicketkeeper, going past former England wicketkeeper Les Ames. With nine hundreds, he is now behind only Adam Gilchrist (17) and Andy Flower (12).Most Test hundreds as a designated wicketkeeper17 – Adam Gilchrist12 – Andy Flower9 – Rishabh Pant8 – Les AmesPant's innings ended when Rachin Ravindra had him caught by Nathan Smith at deep mid-wicket just before lunch. The left-hander struck 10 fours and six sixes, taking his tally of sixes in Test cricket to 108. articles.title: Box-office Rishabh Pant goes on rampage, edges past Brendon McCullum in list of most sixes in Test cricket
articles.summary: Rishabh Pant moved to second place on the list of most sixes in Test cricket, going past former New Zealand batter Brendon McCullum, as he scored his
articles.body: Rishabh Pant moved to second place on the list of most sixes in Test cricket, going past former New Zealand batter Brendon McCullum, as he scored his ninth Test century to help India reach 629 for six at lunch on day four of the opening Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve.Pant struck 10 fours and six sixes during his 128 off 153 balls, taking his tally of sixes in Test cricket to 108. McCullum had hit 107, while England's Ben Stokes tops the list with 138 sixes.Most sixes in Test cricketSixesBatterBalls per six138Ben Stokes90.05108Rishabh Pant47.93107Brendon McCullum93.39100Adam Gilchrist67.9298Jacques Kallis294.8798Chris Gayle122.1198Tim Southee27.70Pant's innings helped India extend their lead to 261 runs by lunch on day four. The visitors added 143 runs in the session after taking control of the match on day three.During his knock, Pant also became the sixth Indian batter, after Sachin Tendulkar, Mohammed Azharuddin, Rahul Dravid, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul, to score a Test century in all four SENA countries. He is also the first Asian wicketkeeper to achieve the feat.Asian batters with Test hundreds in all four SENA countriesMohammad AzharuddinSachin TendulkarSaeed AnwarRahul DravidYounis KhanKumar SangakkaraVirat KohliKL RahulRishabh PantPant began the day cautiously but changed gears after lofting Kyle Jamieson over long-on and sending the ball into the Basin Reserve car park. He then took on off-spinner Glenn Phillips, reaching 99 with a reverse sweep before dancing down the track to hit him over the infield and complete his century.It was the fourth time Pant had reached a Test hundred with a six. He finished with 10 fours and six sixes, sticking to his attacking style despite criticism in recent weeks.Pant's innings was also significant given that he had been out of competitive cricket for seven weeks. He missed the India A matches as well because the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru had not declared him fit to play.There had been questions over whether Pant was ready for a Test match, but his wicketkeeping and batting in the ongoing game have addressed concerns about his form and fitness.FOLLOW LIVEGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ 1st Test: Bossing the Basin! KL Rahul's 13th Test ton, Shubman Gill's 98 put India in command
articles.summary: KL Rahul once again proved his technical proficiency in overseas conditions and marked his maiden Test appearance in New Zealand with a typically measured
articles.body: KL Rahul once again proved his technical proficiency in overseas conditions and marked his maiden Test appearance in New Zealand with a typically measured hundred, before skipper Shubman Gill raised the tempo with a counterattacking and stylish 98 as India tightened their grip on the opening Test at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Saturday.By stumps on Day 3, India, resuming at 159-1, had surged to 486-4 — a lead of 118 — with Rishabh Pant unbeaten on 55. It was an extraordinary collective batting effort, with each of India’s top five crossing fifty in an overseas Test innings for the first time.If Rahul’s 136 off 296 balls, with nine fours and two sixes, laid the foundation, Gill’s 98 off 146 balls, with nine fours and two sixes, provided the impetus. India needed that as they looked to build a lead big enough to avoid batting again and give their bowlers sufficient time to force a result on a placid pitch.Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal (80 off 175; 10x4) carried the momentum from India’s batting effort on Day 2, although the Kiwi bowlers put in an impressive pre-lunch effort. Matt Henry and Nathan Smith operated with ’keeper Tom Blundell standing up to the stumps as Rahul and Padikkal embraced denial and banished extravagance.It meant India’s first run of the morning came only off the 21st delivery and five of the first six overs were maidens. Padikkal completed a composed half-century and Rahul gradually began to open up, even dancing down the track to loft Glenn Phillips over long-on with a shot that almost struck a baby in the stands — much to Rahul’s anguish.Rahul and Padikkal went through the entire first session without being separated, adding 80 in 27 overs.Soon after lunch, Rahul nudged Jacob Duffy for a single to complete his 13th Test century. The India vice-captain became only the fourth Indian, after Sachin Tendulkar, Mohammed Azharuddin and Rahul Dravid, to score Test hundreds in all four SENA countries — South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia — and the first Indian opener to accomplish the feat.The second-wicket partnership had reached 165 when Kyle Jamieson finally produced something special with the second new ball. Bowling from around the wicket, he got one to hold its line and hit the top of Padikkal’s off stump.Gill arrived with intent. Sensing that Rahul had started tiring, the captain looked to push the scoring rate. Rahul eventually dragged a Smith delivery onto his stumps for 136 after adding 91 with Gill.If the hosts thought getting Rahul would provide some respite, they were mistaken. In Rishabh Pant, India had the ideal batter to take advantage of a flagging attack. Initially content to turn the strike over to Gill, Pant exploded once he found his range.In between sporadic coughs and witty barbs, he hooked Duffy for two sixes and a four in one over and raced to his 22nd Test half-century off 55 balls.Gill, meanwhile, continued to attack, using his feet beautifully against spin. India crossed 400 and then pushed their lead beyond 100.The day, however, ended with personal disappointment for Gill. Having spent more than eight overs in the 90s, an overanxious Gill fell two short of his century when Duffy adjusted the square-leg and deep fine-leg fielders to give him the impression that a short ball was coming. Instead, Duffy bowled a full delivery that seamed back in and breached the skipper’s defence.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rishabh Pant creates history, becomes first Indian wicketkeeper to score Test hundreds in all SENA countries
articles.summary: Rishabh Pant added another special achievement to his name on Sunday, becoming the first Indian wicketkeeper to score Test centuries in all four SENA
articles.body: Rishabh Pant added another special achievement to his name on Sunday, becoming the first Indian wicketkeeper to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries - South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.The left-handed batter reached the milestone with an attacking century on Day 4 of the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington.Pant, 29, was playing his first match for India since the tour of Sri Lanka in August. He brought up his hundred in just 135 balls. At 99, he played a cheeky reverse-sweep off part-time spinner Glenn Phillips, sending the ball past short third man. On the very next delivery, he stepped down the track and hit Phillips over mid-off for a six to complete his century.Pant was eventually caught at deep midwicket for 128 off 153 balls. However, his knock had helped India take a 261-run lead by the lunch break.Joins an elite listPant became only the sixth Indian batter to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries. The other five are Mohammad Azharuddin, Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul.Rahul entered the list a day earlier, becoming the first Indian opener to achieve the feat.Asian batters with Test centuries in all four SENA countries:Mohammad AzharuddinSachin TendulkarSaeed AnwarRahul DravidYounis KhanKumar SangakkaraVirat KohliKL RahulRishabh PantPakistan's Saeed Anwar and Younis Khan, along with Sri Lanka's Kumar Sangakkara, are the other Asian batters to have achieved this feat.Among wicketkeepers from around the world, only Australia's Adam Gilchrist and England's Jonny Bairstow have also scored Test hundreds in all four SENA countries.Third on the list of most Test hundreds by wicketkeepersThe Wellington century was Pant's ninth in Test cricket as a designated wicketkeeper. He is now third on the all-time list, behind Gilchrist (17) and Zimbabwe's Andy Flower (12).Seven of Pant's nine Test hundreds have come outside India. He also became the first Indian wicketkeeper to score a Test century in New Zealand.Most Test centuries as a designated wicketkeeper17 – Adam Gilchrist12 – Andy Flower9 – Rishabh Pant8 – Les AmesA look at Pant's SENA centuriesPant's journey of scoring Test hundreds in all four SENA countries began with a 114-run knock at The Oval in 2018.He followed it with an unbeaten 159 against Australia in Sydney in 2019. That remains his highest Test score.In January 2022, he scored an unbeaten 100 in Cape Town against South Africa. Later that year, he hit 146 against England at Edgbaston.Last year, Pant continued his good run in England, scoring 134 and 118 at Leeds.Pant shows no signs of rust after injury breakPant's return to international cricket was closely watched after he missed India's entire four-day series against New Zealand A due to a left-side strain.Before that, he had led Rest of India in the Irani Cup match against Ranji Trophy champions Jammu & Kashmir in Srinagar in October.However, he looked in excellent touch in Wellington and showed no signs of being short of match practice.Pant scored most of his runs on the leg side, using his trademark slog sweeps and powerful shots. He often moved his front leg out of the way to open up the leg-side field and played several shots behind square. He also used his feet well to hit the ball over the bowler's head.Moves past McCullum in Test sixes listPant's attacking century also helped him move past former New Zealand captain Brendon McCullum in the list of most sixes in Test cricket.He now has 108 sixes, putting him second on the list behind England captain Ben Stokes, who has 138.Most sixes in Test cricket138 – Ben Stokes (Balls per six: 90.05)108 – Rishabh Pant (Balls per six: 47.93)107 – Brendon McCullum (Balls per six: 93.39)100 – Adam Gilchrist (Balls per six: 67.92)98 – Jacques Kallis (Balls per six: 294.87)98 – Chris Gayle (Balls per six: 122.11)98 – Tim Southee (Balls per six: 27.70)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 720/9! Team India rewrite record books, post highest-ever Test total in New Zealand
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India delivered a remarkable batting performance against New Zealand in the first Test at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Sunday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India delivered a remarkable batting performance against New Zealand in the first Test at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Sunday. The visitors declared their innings at 720/9 on Day 4, building a massive 352-run lead.In the process, India registered the highest-ever team total in a Test innings in New Zealand. They broke the previous record of 715/6 declared, which the hosts had scored against Bangladesh in Hamilton in 2019.KL Rahul and Rishabh Pant were the stars with the bat, scoring 136 and 128 respectively. Glenn Phillips was the most successful New Zealand bowler, finishing with figures of 3/154.India declared their innings around an hour before tea, with Dhruv Jurel being the last batter to get out. New Zealand had scored 368 in their first innings, leaving them with a huge challenge after India's batting effort.India set new record for highest Test total in New ZealandIndia's 720/9 became the biggest total ever scored in a Test innings on New Zealand soil. The previous best was the hosts' 715/6 declared against Bangladesh in Hamilton in 2019.India also broke the record for the highest Test total against New Zealand. The West Indies had earlier held the record with their 660/5 declared at the Basin Reserve in Wellington in 1995.India's highest Test totals against New Zealand720/9 declared – Wellington, 2026 (Won)583/7 declared – Ahmedabad, 1999 (Draw)566/8 declared – Nagpur, 2010 (Won)557/5 declared – Indore, 2016 (Won)537/3 declared – Chennai, 1956 (Won)India had crossed 500 runs in a Test innings in New Zealand only once before this match. They scored 520 all out against the hosts in Hamilton in 2009.Six consecutive 50-plus partnershipsIndia's innings also featured a rare batting record. Each of their first six partnerships added at least 50 runs.This has happened only four times in Test cricket. Australia first achieved it against West Indies in Brisbane in 1960-61. Pakistan followed with a similar effort against Bangladesh in Khulna in 2015.India also managed the feat against Australia in Ahmedabad in 2023. Their performance in Wellington makes them the first team to achieve it twice.Another unusual record came from India's top five batters, with each of them scoring at least 80 runs. This has happened only twice in Test cricket.The previous occasion was in 2014, when Pakistan's top five all scored 80 or more in their innings of 566/3 declared against New Zealand in Abu Dhabi.India second on list of most 700-plus Test totalsIndia's 720/9 was their fifth 700-plus score in Test cricket. They now occupy the second position on the list of teams with the most 700-plus totals.Sri Lanka lead the chart with seven such scores. India have five, while England, Australia and West Indies have four each.Most 700-plus totals in Test cricket7 – Sri Lanka5 – India4 – England4 – Australia4 – West Indies2 – Pakistan1 – New ZealandIndia's third-highest Test totalThe 720-run effort in Wellington is now India's third-highest total in Test cricket.Their biggest score remains 759/7 declared against England in Chennai in 2016. The second-highest is 726/9 declared against Sri Lanka at the Brabourne Stadium in 2009.India's highest innings totals in Test cricket759/7 declared vs England – Chennai, 2016726/9 declared vs Sri Lanka – Brabourne, 2009720/9 declared vs New Zealand – Wellington, 2026707 vs Sri Lanka – Colombo (SSC), 2010705/7 declared vs Australia – Sydney, 2004Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
